tara: Strange one: our Next.js middleware started throwing in preview: "TypeError: globalThis.fetch is not a function" when importing the SDK normally. Local dev works. Anyone seen globalThis weirdness?
ben: Yup. Usually a bundler/resolution issue where the wrong entrypoint brings in a tiny node polyfill that overwrites fetch with an incomplete shim. That shim can lack clone/stream helpers.
li: We had the same after importing the main package. Fix was to add an explicit edge export and point Vercel to dist/edge.mjs. Also ensure the edge build doesn't import node utils at top-level.
li: Example package.json snippet we used:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},
  "./edge": "./dist/edge.mjs"
}
```
tara: Worked when I switched to `import('redwood-inference/edge')` lazily inside middleware. But TS still complained: "Cannot find name 'Request'" because the project pulled @types/node globally.
sam: Two complementary fixes: 1) ship an edge.d.ts that references only DOM libs, 2) docs showing tsconfig override for middleware: add "lib": ["esnext","dom"]. That avoids Node types bleeding into the middleware compile.
ops-bot: reminder: ci/edge-sanity failing for main because dist/edge.mjs pulled in util.inspect via logger.
ben: For logger we lazy-import on node-only paths: `if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.release?.name === 'node') await import('./node-logger')`. Keeps edge bundle clean.
li: Also, replace setTimeout-based retry in edge build with AbortController/timeouts. Worker environments don't guarantee timers and that caused hung retries for us.
tara: Thanks — I'll open an issue with repro + a minimal middleware showing lazy import and tsconfig tweak. Will validate preview once the edge export lands. :white_check_mark:
